newsitem.title: USA: Dun & Bradstreet seeks 5-7 pct net growth.
newsitem.headline: Dun & Bradstreet seeks 5-7 pct net growth.

text.p: Dun & Bradstreet Corp on Thursday said its goal this year was to produce five to seven percent more net income than in 1996 on adjusted basis.
Volney Taylor, chairman and chief executive officer, said the company could focus its full attention on improving its 1997 results now that its reorganization was complete.
"We are off to a strong start this year," he said.
The company, which completed the spin-offs of Cognizant Corp and ACNielsen Corp on November 1, said 1996 revenues on an adjusted basis rose five percent to $2.09 billion from $1.99 billion.
The company, which provides commercial credit and business marketing information, said adjusted full-year earnings rose to $285 million, or $1.68 a share, from $277 million, or $1.63.
"The earnings on an adjusted basis were in line with prior estimates," Taylor said.
Analysts on average had forecast 1996 earnings of $1.68 on an adjusted basis, according to a First Call survey.
The company said results on an adjusted basis exclude the one-time transaction costs associated with the reorganization, other non-recurring items and the results of divested businesses.
Results on an adjusted basis also reflect the company's expected overhead and interest run-rate expenses, as well as a new underlying tax rate of 34 percent, it said.

For the fourth quarter, earnings per share were $0.86 on an adjusted basis, including a gain of $0.31 related to an accounting change in recognizing revenue generated by its directory information segment, effective January 1, 1996.

In the fourth quarter, it said it changed to the predominant industry practice of reporting revenue and related expenses at the time the Yellow Pages directories are published. Previously, revenue and related expenses were reported ratably during the year.
The company said the change had no impact on the full year results either on a reported or as adjusted basis.

The company reported a fourth-quarter loss of $115.9 million, or $.68 per share, versus a loss in the year-earlier period of $105.7 million, or $.62. In both cases, the results included the accounting change.
The company said its net debt was about $1.0 billion at the end of 1996, within the range previously estimated.

Shareholders' equity was negative about $432 million at the end of the year. The negative equity position was the result of one-time items associated with the spin-offs and divestiture activity. It would have no impact on the company's future cash flows or operating results, it said.
Without the fourth-quarter change, adjusted earnings would have been flat over the year-earlier period.
On a reported or Form 10K basis, the company showed a consolidated 1996 loss of $44.4 million, or $.26 per share, compared with net income of $320.8 million, or $1.89, in the previous year.

The 1996 results reflect non-recurring charges of $492 million after tax incurred for transactions and divestitures relating to the spin-offs of Cognizant and ACNielsen and the sale of certain businesses, it said.
